dynamic programming essential for optimizing syntactic parsing in this context? Q7. [5 Marks]
Differentiate between syntactic parsing and semantic analysis. Provide a linguistic example where a
syntactically correct and perfectly parsed sentence is entirely semantically anomalous. Q8. [5 Marks]
What are the primary differences between Recursive Transition Networks (RTNs) and Finite State
Automata (FSAs) in modeling natural language grammar? Discuss why FSAs fail to model nested linguistic
structures. Q9. [5 Marks]
Discuss the role of pragmatic analysis in modern conversational agents. Why is coreference resolution
vital for maintaining dialogue state and conversational context? Q10.

6.content:
[5 Marks]
Ambiguity represents one of the most significant challenges in natural language understanding. Categorize and explain at least three types of linguistic ambiguity (e.g., lexical, syntactic, semantic) using
original sentence examples. Q3. [5 Marks]
Describe the structural components of a modern computational lexicon. How does the choice of
underlying data structures (such as Tries or Hash Maps) impact the computational efficiency of lexicon lookups
during real-time processing? Q4. [5 Marks]
Compare and contrast Rule-Based Machine Translation (RBMT) architectures with Statistical Machine
Translation (SMT) frameworks, highlighting their respective dependencies on lexicons versus parallel corpora. Q5. [5 Marks]
Analyze the specific complexities introduced by free word order and extensive morphological richness
when developing efficient NLP parsers for Indian languages (such as Hindi, Tamil, or Marathi). Q6. [5 Marks]
